title: The Pen and the Inkstand

full_text:
In a poet's study, the inkstand and the quill pen engaged in a furious dispute. "All the marvelous poems and great books come from my black ink!" boasted the inkstand. "Without my ink, the world would have no literature!"

"Nonsense!" rasped the goose quill. "Without my sharp nib and delicate stroke, your ink would be mere dirty puddle! I guide the words across the white paper!"

The poet entered. He dipped the pen into the inkstand and wrote a sublime hymn praising the Creator: "Man is but a humble flute upon which the Divine breathes harmony. The instrument is nothing; the Master Musician is everything."

The poet went to sleep. The pen and inkstand sat in silent shame on the desk, realizing that neither ink nor quill created the poetry, but the living soul that guided them both.
moral: The instrument must not boast of the music; all inspiration flows from the Master's hand.
